traces.question_stem: Two identical lamps, L1 and L2, are connected in series to a 6V battery. Explain why L1 and L2 will or will not have the same brightness.
traces.synthetic_student_scratchpad: Okay, the circuit starts at the positive terminal of the 6V battery. Current flows out into L1. Inside L1, it uses up some of the current to light up the filament. So L1 gets full current, let's say 2 Amps. Then the rest of the current that wasn't used leaves L1 and enters L2. Since some was already used by L1, L2 gets less current, maybe 1 Amp. Therefore, L1 will be brighter and L2 will be dimmer because current gets exhausted as it travels along the wire.

rest of the current that wasn't used

traces.question_stem: If you cover the bottom half of a convex lens with black tape, what happens to the image of an object formed on a screen?
traces.synthetic_student_scratchpad: A convex lens works like a window. When light passes through, the top half of the lens makes the top of the image and the bottom half makes the bottom of the image. If I put black tape over the bottom half, no light can go through the bottom half of the glass. That means the rays that make the bottom part of the object can't reach the screen. So the bottom half of the image will be blocked and won't appear on the screen at all.
key_linguistic_markers: top half makes the top, bottom half makes the bottom
bottom half of the image will be blocked

traces.question_stem: A 9V battery powers a single 3-ohm resistor. If we connect another 3-ohm resistor in parallel across the first, what is the total current leaving the battery?
traces.synthetic_student_scratchpad: The battery is a 9V battery. In the first case, I = 9/3 = 3 Amps. The battery always produces 3 Amps because it is a 9V battery with 3A capacity. When you add another 3-ohm resistor in parallel, the battery still gives 3 Amps total, but now that 3 Amps has to split: 1.5 Amps goes to the first resistor and 1.5 Amps goes to the second resistor. So the total current from the battery doesn't change, it stays 3 Amps.
key_linguistic_markers: total current from the battery doesn't change

traces.question_stem: A proton at rest is placed near the North pole of a strong bar magnet. Describe what force it experiences.
traces.synthetic_student_scratchpad: A proton has a positive charge (+1.6 * 10^-19 C). The North pole of a magnet is positive and the South pole is negative, like in electrostatics. Since like charges repel each other, the positive proton will feel a strong repulsive electrostatic force pushing it directly away from the North pole.
key_linguistic_markers: North pole of a magnet is positive
